tasks.title: Scaffold the runstat package with both entry points
tasks.goal: Nothing else in this plan can be run until there is a project uv can execute. This task creates the Python project (src/ layout, standard library only at runtime, pytest as the sole dev dependency) and a CLI that already knows its three subcommands, so every later task extends a working program instead of inventing one. The three subcommands may be stubs here; the point is that `runstat` and `python -m runstat` both resolve and both advertise summary, signals and compare.
acceptance: pyproject.toml declares a project named runstat with an empty runtime dependency list and a console script entry point named `runstat`.
pytest is declared as a development dependency and `uv run pytest` resolves it; no other dependency is added anywhere.
The package lives under src/runstat/ and `uv run python -c "import runstat"` succeeds.
`uv run runstat --help` and `uv run python -m runstat --help` both exit 0 and both list the subcommands summary, signals and compare.
No file added by this task contains an absolute path.
tasks.verify: uv run python -c 'import runstat' && uv run python -m runstat --help >/dev/null && uv run runstat --help >/dev/null && uv run runstat --help | grep -q summary && uv run runstat --help | grep -q signals && uv run runstat --help | grep -q compare && uv run python -c 'import pytest' && python3 -c "import tomllib,pathlib; d=tomllib.loads(pathlib.Path('pyproject.toml').read_text()); assert d['project'].get('dependencies',[])==[], d['project'].get('dependencies'); assert 'runstat' in d['project'].get('scripts',{}), d['project'].get('scripts')"

tasks.title: Check in the two fixture run directories the gates read
tasks.goal: Every later gate needs a run directory with known-correct numbers, and the brief's worked example is the arbiter for all of them. This task lays that data on disk: run 20260814-101500 exactly as the brief's table specifies, plus a second, smaller run 20260815-090000 used as the comparison variant so `compare` and the README examples are reproducible. These are read-only inputs; pytest tests must still build their own runs inside tmp_path and must never write into these directories or into loop/runs.
acceptance: tests/fixtures/runs/20260814-101500/sessions/ holds exactly the seven files named in the brief's worked example, each with the phase, iteration, total_cost_usd, num_turns and duration_ms from that table, is_error false and an empty permission_denials list.
tests/fixtures/runs/20260814-101500/iterations.jsonl holds exactly the three records printed in the brief, in that order.

tests/fixtures/runs/20260815-090000/ is a second, valid run: five sessions — 001-plan.json (plan, 0, 2.10, 14, 150000), 002-work.json (work, 1, 0.60, 8, 80000), 003-review.json (review, 1, 0.20, 3, 25000), 004-work.json (work, 2, 0.55, 6, 70000), 005-review.json (review, 2, 0.20, 3, 25000) — all with is_error false and empty permission_denials.

tests/fixtures/runs/20260815-090000/iterations.jsonl holds exactly two records: {"iteration": 1, "task": "T1", "outcome": "done", "attempts": 0, "tasks_done": 1, "tasks_total": 8} then {"iteration": 2, "task": "T2", "outcome": "review_fail", "attempts": 1, "tasks_done": 1, "tasks_total": 8}.
Session files may carry additional keys from a real result JSON (session_id, usage, result and so on), but nothing that holds message content beyond the result field, and no absolute paths.
tasks.verify:
python3 -c "
import json,pathlib
A='tests/fixtures/runs/20260814-101500'
B='tests/fixtures/runs/20260815-090000'
exp={A:[('001-plan.json','plan',0,1.98,12,141000),('002-work.json','work',1,0.5,6,68000),('003-review.json','review',1,0.2,3,24000),('004-work.json','work',2,0.52,7,72000),('005-review.json','review',2,0.2,3,24000),('006-work.json','work',3,0.48,5,64000),('007-review.json','review',3,0.2,3,24000)],B:[('001-plan.json','plan',0,2.1,14,150000),('002-work.json','work',1,0.6,8,80000),('003-review.json','review',1,0.2,3,25000),('004-work.json','work',2,0.55,6,70000),('005-review.json','review',2,0.2,3,25000)]}
recs={A:[{'iteration':1,'task':'T1','outcome':'done','attempts':0,'tasks_done':1,'tasks_total':8},{'iteration':2,'task':'T2','outcome':'gate_fail','attempts':1,'tasks_done':1,'tasks_total':8},{'iteration':3,'task':'T2','outcome':'done','attempts':1,'tasks_done':2,'tasks_total':8}],B:[{'iteration':1,'task':'T1','outcome':'done','attempts':0,'tasks_done':1,'tasks_total':8},{'iteration':2,'task':'T2','outcome':'review_fail','attempts':1,'tasks_done':1,'tasks_total':8}]}
for run,rows in exp.items():
    d=pathlib.Path(run)
    assert sorted(p.name for p in (d/'sessions').glob('*.json'))==[r[0] for r in rows], run
    for name,phase,it,cost,turns,dur in rows:
        s=json.loads((d/'sessions'/name).read_text())
        assert (s['phase'],s['iteration'],round(float(s['total_cost_usd']),2),s['num_turns'],s['duration_ms'])==(phase,it,cost,turns,dur), (run,name)
        assert s['is_error'] is False and s['permission_denials']==[], (run,name)
    got=[json.loads(x) for x in (d/'iterations.jsonl').read_text().splitlines() if x.strip()]
    assert got==recs[run], (run,got)
print('fixtures ok')
"

tasks.title: Implement runstat summary — the per-phase rollup
tasks.goal: This is the first command that reads telemetry off disk, so it also brings in whatever loading and parsing the rest of the tool will share. It reports one row per phase — session count, total cost, total turns, total wall time — plus a total row, over the run directory it is given. The brief's worked-example table is the exact expected output; column widths and padding are yours to choose, the numbers, labels and their pairing are not.
acceptance: `runstat summary tests/fixtures/runs/20260814-101500` exits 0 and prints rows for plan (1 session, $1.98, 12 turns, 141s), work (3, $1.50, 18, 204s), review (3, $0.60, 9, 72s) and a total row (7, $4.08, 39, 417s).
Rows appear in the column order the brief's table uses: phase, sessions, cost, turns, wall.
Costs print as dollars to two decimals; wall time prints as whole seconds with an `s` suffix.
The output says somewhere that the dollar figures are an estimate.
Sessions are grouped by their `phase` key; a run directory is read from `sessions/*.json` under the directory given on the command line.
The tool imports nothing outside the standard library.
tasks.verify:
o="$(uv run runstat summary tests/fixtures/runs/20260814-101500)" || exit 1; printf '%s
' "$o" | grep -qE '^plan[[:space:]|]+1[[:space:]|]+\$1\.98[[:space:]|]+12[[:space:]|]+141s[[:space:]|]*$' && printf '%s
' "$o" | grep -qE '^work[[:space:]|]+3[[:space:]|]+\$1\.50[[:space:]|]+18[[:space:]|]+204s[[:space:]|]*$' && printf '%s
' "$o" | grep -qE '^review[[:space:]|]+3[[:space:]|]+\$0\.60[[:space:]|]+9[[:space:]|]+72s[[:space:]|]*$' && printf '%s
' "$o" | grep -qE '^[Tt]otal[[:space:]|]+7[[:space:]|]+\$4\.08[[:space:]|]+39[[:space:]|]+417s[[:space:]|]*$' && printf '%s
' "$o" | grep -qi estimat

tasks.title: Call out error sessions and permission denials in summary
tasks.goal: A permission denial the operator never sees is a fence in the wrong place that nobody knows about, and a crashed session hidden inside a phase total is the same problem. summary must name the offending session files rather than just folding them into the rollup. This is not an error condition: a run with a denial in it is still a readable run, so the exit code stays 0 and the rollup still prints.
acceptance: A session whose `is_error` is true is called out in summary's output, identified by its file name.
A session whose `permission_denials` is a non-empty list is called out in summary's output, identified by its file name, and the call-out says these are denials.
Both call-outs happen in the same run when both conditions are present, and the per-phase rollup still prints.
A run where every session has is_error false and empty permission_denials prints no call-out and still exits 0.
summary exits 0 in all of these cases — an error session is something to report, not a failure to read the run.
tasks.verify:
d="$(mktemp -d)" && cp -R tests/fixtures/runs/20260814-101500 "$d/flag" && python3 -c "import json,pathlib,sys; s=pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1])/'sessions'; a=json.loads((s/'004-work.json').read_text()); a['is_error']=True; (s/'004-work.json').write_text(json.dumps(a)); b=json.loads((s/'006-work.json').read_text()); b['permission_denials']=['Bash(git push:*)']; (s/'006-work.json').write_text(json.dumps(b))" "$d/flag" && o="$(uv run runstat summary "$d/flag")" && printf '%s
' "$o" | grep -q '004-work.json' && printf '%s
' "$o" | grep -q '006-work.json' && printf '%s
' "$o" | grep -qi denial && printf '%s
' "$o" | grep -qi error && ! uv run runstat summary tests/fixtures/runs/20260814-101500 | grep -qi denial

tasks.title: Implement runstat signals — the eight run-level signals
tasks.goal: These eight numbers are the only thing that makes a run visible from outside itself, and the loop driver computes the same eight inline while a run is in flight. Brief 0002 acceptance item 6 requires the two implementations to agree exactly on a completed run, so the derivations in the brief's table are not free choices — a formula that is merely reasonable but different is a defect. Note especially that attempts burned counts records whose outcome is not `done`, and is not the sum of the `attempts` field.
acceptance: Output is one `key: value` line per signal, using exactly the labels in the brief: iterations, tasks closed, iterations per closed, gate failures, review rejections, attempts burned, no-progress streak, estimated spend.
`runstat signals tests/fixtures/runs/20260814-101500` exits 0 and prints exactly the values 3, 2/8, 1.50, 1, 0, 1, 0 and $4.08 against those labels, in that order.
iterations per closed is iterations divided by tasks closed to two decimals, and is the literal string `n/a` when zero tasks are closed.
attempts burned counts iterations.jsonl records whose outcome is not `done` — it is not the sum of the per-record `attempts` field.
no-progress streak counts the trailing records whose tasks_done did not increase over the previous record.
tasks closed reads tasks_done and tasks_total from the last record of iterations.jsonl.
estimated spend sums total_cost_usd across all session files and is labelled as an estimate by its own label.
tasks.verify:
o="$(uv run runstat signals tests/fixtures/runs/20260814-101500)" || exit 1; printf '%s
' "$o" | grep -qE '^iterations:[[:space:]]+3$' && printf '%s
' "$o" | grep -qE '^tasks closed:[[:space:]]+2/8$' && printf '%s
' "$o" | grep -qE '^iterations per closed:[[:space:]]+1\.50$' && printf '%s
' "$o" | grep -qE '^gate failures:[[:space:]]+1$' && printf '%s
' "$o" | grep -qE '^review rejections:[[:space:]]+0$' && printf '%s
' "$o" | grep -qE '^attempts burned:[[:space:]]+1$' && printf '%s
' "$o" | grep -qE '^no-progress streak:[[:space:]]+0$' && printf '%s
' "$o" | grep -qE '^estimated spend:[[:space:]]+\$4\.08$' && uv run runstat signals tests/fixtures/runs/20260815-090000 | grep -qE '^iterations per closed:[[:space:]]+2\.00$'

tasks.title: Implement runstat compare — two runs side by side with deltas
tasks.goal: This is the repeatability check: two runs of the same plan should show comparable signals, and a large divergence is the finding. It prints every signal from `signals` for both runs with a delta column, so it must reuse the same derivations rather than recomputing them differently. The delta is the second run minus the first; signals that are not numeric, such as tasks closed, get a blank delta rather than a placeholder.
acceptance: `runstat compare <run-a> <run-b>` prints one line per signal, with the signal's label, its value for run A, its value for run B, and a delta.
Every signal that `signals` prints appears in compare, with the same labels.
Numeric deltas are the second run's value minus the first's, formatted to the same precision as the signal itself, with an explicit leading `+` when positive.
Non-numeric signals — tasks closed — get a blank delta column, not `n/a` or `0`.

Against tests/fixtures/runs/20260814-101500 and tests/fixtures/runs/20260815-090000 the deltas are: iterations -1, iterations per closed +0.50, gate failures -1, review rejections +1, attempts burned 0, no-progress streak +1, and estimated spend a drop of 0.43.
compare exits 0 when both run directories are readable.
tasks.verify:
A=tests/fixtures/runs/20260814-101500; B=tests/fixtures/runs/20260815-090000; o="$(uv run runstat compare $A $B)" || exit 1; printf '%s
' "$o" | grep -qE '^iterations:?[[:space:]|]+3[[:space:]|]+2[[:space:]|]+-1[[:space:]|]*$' && printf '%s
' "$o" | grep -qE '^iterations per closed:?[[:space:]|]+1\.50[[:space:]|]+2\.00[[:space:]|]+\+0\.50[[:space:]|]*$' && printf '%s
' "$o" | grep -qE '^tasks closed:?[[:space:]|]+2/8[[:space:]|]+1/8[[:space:]|]*$' && printf '%s
' "$o" | grep -qE '^review rejections:?[[:space:]|]+0[[:space:]|]+1[[:space:]|]+\+1[[:space:]|]*$' && printf '%s
' "$o" | grep -qE '^gate failures:?[[:space:]|]+1[[:space:]|]+0[[:space:]|]+-1[[:space:]|]*$' && printf '%s
' "$o" | grep -qE '^no-progress streak:?[[:space:]|]+0[[:space:]|]+1[[:space:]|]+\+1[[:space:]|]*$' && printf '%s
' "$o" | grep -qE '^estimated spend:?[[:space:]|]+\$4\.08[[:space:]|]+\$3\.65.*0\.43'

tasks.title: Enforce the exit-code and error contract across all three commands
tasks.goal: A partial result indistinguishable from a correct one is the failure mode this whole tool exists to catch, so a malformed session file or iterations.jsonl line must be a loud refusal, never a silent skip. This task makes every command obey one contract: 0 on success, 1 when the run directory is valid but holds no sessions, 2 for a usage error, a missing directory or malformed input — with the offending path on stderr, stdout empty, and no traceback ever reaching the user.
acceptance: A run directory that does not exist exits 2 with a message on stderr and empty stdout.
A single unparseable file in sessions/ exits 2 and names that file's path on stderr; the same holds for one unparseable line of iterations.jsonl, which names iterations.jsonl.
A malformed record is never skipped and never produces a partial report.
A valid run directory containing no session files exits 1, with the explanation on stderr and empty stdout.
Invoking with no subcommand, an unknown subcommand, or the wrong number of arguments exits 2 with a usage message on stderr.
No invocation prints a Python traceback; all error text goes to stderr and stdout stays empty whenever the exit code is non-zero.
All three commands share this behaviour.
tasks.verify: d="$(mktemp -d)" && A=tests/fixtures/runs/20260814-101500 && mkdir -p "$d/empty/sessions" && : >"$d/empty/iterations.jsonl" && cp -R $A "$d/badsess" && printf '{' >"$d/badsess/sessions/002-work.json" && cp -R $A "$d/baditer" && printf 'not json\n' >>"$d/baditer/iterations.jsonl" && chk() { e=$1; shift; uv run runstat "$@" >"$d/o" 2>"$d/e"; rc=$?; [ "$rc" = "$e" ] || { echo "want exit $e got $rc for: $*"; return 1; }; [ -s "$d/o" ] && { echo "stdout not empty for: $*"; return 1; }; [ -s "$d/e" ] || { echo "stderr empty for: $*"; return 1; }; grep -q Traceback "$d/e" && { echo "traceback for: $*"; return 1; }; return 0; } && chk 2 && chk 2 bogus "$A" && chk 2 compare "$A" && chk 2 summary "$d/nope" && chk 2 signals "$d/nope" && chk 2 summary "$d/badsess" && chk 2 signals "$d/badsess" && chk 2 signals "$d/baditer" && chk 2 compare "$A" "$d/baditer" && chk 1 summary "$d/empty" && chk 1 signals "$d/empty" && uv run runstat summary "$d/badsess" 2>&1 >/dev/null | grep -q '002-work.json' && uv run runstat signals "$d/baditer" 2>&1 >/dev/null | grep -q 'iterations.jsonl'

tasks.title: Write the pytest suite, including the worked example end to end
tasks.goal: The gates check the tool from outside; this suite is what keeps it honest as it changes. It must include the brief's worked example as a single end-to-end test — the one test that catches an implementation whose parts each pass in isolation while the whole drifts — alongside per-command and error-contract tests. Every test builds its run directories inside pytest's tmp_path; nothing reads or writes a real run directory under loop/runs.
acceptance: `uv run pytest -q` exits 0 with at least ten tests passing and none failing.
One test drives the brief's worked example end to end and asserts summary's per-phase numbers, signals' eight values, and a compare delta on at least one numeric signal.
Tests cover the error contract: missing directory, malformed session file, malformed iterations.jsonl line, and a run with no sessions, each asserted on exit code and on stderr.
Every test writes only inside pytest's tmp_path; no test references loop/runs or any absolute path.
Tests assert on content, not on column alignment, for summary and compare; signals values are asserted exactly.
tasks.verify: out="$(uv run pytest -q 2>&1)"; printf '%s\n' "$out" | tail -3; printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qE '^[0-9]{2,} passed' && grep -rq tmp_path tests && grep -rq '4\.08' tests && ! grep -rq 'loop/runs' tests

tasks.title: Write README.md with examples replayed from the tool
tasks.goal: A README whose examples have drifted is worse than none, because a reader trusts it. This one documents what runstat is, how to install and run it with uv, all three commands with worked examples, the exit-code contract and the input layout it reads — and its gate replays the tool against the checked-in fixture runs and requires every line the tool prints to appear verbatim in the file. Use tests/fixtures/runs/20260814-101500 and tests/fixtures/runs/20260815-090000 as the example inputs so a reader can reproduce every example exactly.
acceptance: README.md explains what runstat is and states that it has no runtime role in the loop — it is post-hoc analysis over archived runs.
It shows how to install and run with uv, including both `uv run runstat ...` and `uv run python -m runstat ...`.
It documents all three commands, each with a worked example whose command line and full output are copied from an actual run against the checked-in fixtures.
Every output line shown for summary, signals and compare matches what the tool prints today, character for character.
It states the exit-code contract — 0 success, 1 valid run directory with no sessions, 2 usage error, missing directory or malformed input.
It describes the input layout: <run-id>/sessions/*.json and <run-id>/iterations.jsonl, and the fields read from each.
It says the dollar figures are estimates, not a bill.
It contains no absolute paths.
tasks.verify: d="$(mktemp -d)" && A=tests/fixtures/runs/20260814-101500 && B=tests/fixtures/runs/20260815-090000 && uv run runstat summary $A >"$d/all" && uv run runstat signals $A >>"$d/all" && uv run runstat compare $A $B >>"$d/all" && n=0 && while IFS= read -r l; do [ -z "$l" ] && continue; grep -qF -- "$l" README.md || { echo "README is missing this line the tool prints: $l"; exit 1; }; n=$((n+1)); done <"$d/all" && [ "$n" -ge 20 ] && grep -q 'uv run runstat' README.md && grep -q 'python -m runstat' README.md && grep -q 'iterations.jsonl' README.md && grep -qi estimat README.md && grep -q 'exit' README.md

tasks.title: Write docs/runstat.md, the telemetry contract
tasks.goal: The loop driver computes the same eight signals inline that runstat computes afterwards, and brief 0002 acceptance item 6 requires the two to agree exactly. A derivation recorded in only one implementation is how that agreement quietly breaks, so this document is the shared reference: the telemetry layout field by field, and each signal's derivation written out. It must state the attempts-burned trap explicitly — that the signal counts records whose outcome is not done, and is not the sum of the cumulative per-task attempts field.
acceptance: docs/runstat.md documents the run directory layout — sessions/*.json and iterations.jsonl — and states that session file names are name-sortable in run order.
It documents every session field runstat reads: phase, iteration, total_cost_usd, num_turns, duration_ms, is_error, permission_denials.
It documents the six keys of an iterations.jsonl record and the four legal outcome values: done, gate_fail, review_fail, blocked.
It gives the derivation of all eight signals, matching what the code computes.

It states the attempts-burned trap explicitly: the signal counts records whose outcome is not done, and summing the cumulative per-record attempts field would double-count a task appearing in several records.
It names brief 0002 as the other implementation of these derivations and says the two must agree.
It contains no absolute paths.
tasks.verify: f=docs/runstat.md; test -f $f && for k in 'sessions/' 'iterations.jsonl' 'total_cost_usd' 'num_turns' 'duration_ms' 'is_error' 'permission_denials' 'gate_fail' 'review_fail' 'blocked' 'iterations per closed' 'attempts burned' 'no-progress streak' 'estimated spend' 'tasks closed' 'gate failures' 'review rejections' '0002'; do grep -qF -- "$k" $f || { echo "docs/runstat.md does not mention: $k"; exit 1; }; done; grep -qiE 'cumulative|double-count|double count' $f
